security_spec.violation_condition: QEMU's aes64ks1i helper applies ror32 BEFORE SubBytes and uses the full AES round function (aesenc_SB_SR_AK with ShiftRows) when the corrected spec mandates SubBytes-first-then-rotate with no ShiftRows. For rnum == 0xA, QEMU skips rotation and uses XOR with zero-valued round key, but still applies ShiftRows, while the corrected spec requires only aes_subword_fwd with neither rotation nor rcon XOR. Additionally, trans_aes64ks1i rejects rnum > 0xA as illegal, but the spec now defines valid (zero-valued) rcon entries for 0xB-0xF, changing the illegal-instruction boundary.
security_spec.summary: QEMU applies ror32 before SubBytes (old spec order) and uses full AES round with ShiftRows, but the corrected SAIL spec does SubBytes first then rotate without ShiftRows — all rnum values produce diverging cipher output, corrupting guest key schedule generation

findings.finding: ror32-before-SubBytes order violation: The helper applies ror32(temp, 8) at line 153 BEFORE calling aesenc_SB_SR_AK at line 158. The corrected SAIL spec mandates SubBytes-first-then-rotate. This produces a different output for all rnum != 0xA because rotating first shuffles bytes into different positions before the S-box lookup, yielding wrong S-box outputs per byte position.

ShiftRows incorrectly applied: aesenc_SB_SR_AK (SubBytes+ShiftRows+AddRoundKey) is used at line 158, but the corrected spec requires only SubBytes (aes_subword_fwd) with no ShiftRows. The ShiftRows permutation (AES_SH macro: byte[i] -> byte[(i*5) & 15]) is unconditionally applied, corrupting the key schedule output. For rnum==0xA, ShiftRows is still applied despite no rotation and zero round key, whereas the spec requires only aes_subword_fwd with neither ShiftRows nor rcon XOR.

aesenc_SB_SR_AK(&t, &t, &rc, false);

findings.finding: rnum==0xA special-case mismatch: When rnum==0xA, the helper skips rotation and sets rc to zero (implicit via ={}), so the AddRoundKey XOR becomes a no-op. However aesenc_SB_SR_AK still applies ShiftRows on the SubBytes output. The corrected spec requires only aes_subword_fwd (pure SubBytes) for rnum==0xA, with no ShiftRows and no rcon XOR.

Illegal-instruction boundary too restrictive: The translate function rejects rnum > 0xA as illegal (return false at line 132). The updated spec defines valid rcon entries for rnum 0xB-0xF (zero-valued), meaning these are legal instruction encodings that should execute. Additionally, the round_consts[] table only has 10 entries, so extending the boundary would also require extending the table to avoid out-of-bounds reads.
